comments.body: Fix pushed as Gerrit change 3181 (commit 81172cf6171). Evidence: (1) Before: a scratch pytest plugin that SIGSTOPs the test process 0.1 s into the call phase and SIGCONTs it 4.5 s later failed the unmodified test 3 of 3 on py3.11.16 with 'assert cancelled' passing and 'assert elapsed < 4.5' failing at 4.63-4.66 s; the read-timeout probe failed the same way. (2) Code path: 200 in-suite samples (full unit tier on py3.11, -n 4 --dist worksteal) plus 50 under 40-48 bounded busy workers: cancel 0.300-0.303 s after tool start in every sample, run end at most 0.48 s, GC inside the run at most 0.003 s, no leftover tasks on the reused event loop. (3) After: same freeze, 3 of 3 pass; a 6 s freeze also passes. (4) Mutations: dropping tool_timeout=0.3 fails 'assert cancelled'; read=5 with the server releasing at 1 s fails the ReadTimeout assert; restored file passes. (5) py3.11 -n 4 3 of 3 pass; make lint exit 0 (wall-clock-asserts clean); make typecheck exit 0.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py::test_tool_timeout_cancels_an_async_tool` failed CI's
`pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.11)` cell on Gerrit change 3177 patch set 1
(run https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/41236108209, job 124640532173),
voting `Verified -1` on a change that touches only `scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py` and its
test file:

```
assert cancelled            # passed
>       assert elapsed < 4.5
E       assert 4.775286564999988 < 4.5
tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py:268: AssertionError
```

The same cell passed on change 3176 about an hour earlier, so the failure is intermittent.

## Root cause (reproduced)

The `elapsed < 4.5` bound measures whole-process wall time around `agent.run_sync`, not
cancellation. The cancellation itself is prompt and does not wait on anything:

- 200 in-suite samples (py3.11.16, full unit tier, `-n 4 --dist worksteal`, the test's exact run
  replayed every 100 tests on each worker) plus 50 samples under 40-48 bounded busy workers
  (including the probe at `nice 20`): the cancel lands 0.300-0.303 s after the tool starts in
  every sample, the whole run ends by 0.48 s at most (median 0.31 s), and GC time inside the run
  is at most 0.003 s.
- Freezing the test process for 4.5 s (SIGSTOP/SIGCONT from a bounded helper 0.1 s into the call
  phase, simulating a descheduled CI worker) reproduces the CI signature 3 of 3 runs on py3.11:
  `assert cancelled` passes and `assert elapsed < 4.5` fails at 4.63-4.66 s.
- The same CI run shows worker-wide stalls of that order: a fixture that only sets environment
  variables (`_default_jira_project`, `tests/unit/reconciler/conftest.py:27`) took 1.751 s on gw1,
  reported by the `[rebar-ci-timing]` warning.

So the defect is in the test: a 4.5 s ceiling against a 5 s failure mode leaves 0.5 s of slack for
host stalls. The sibling `test_stalled_server_trips_read_timeout_under_run_sync` has the same
shape (`elapsed < 4.5` against a 5 s server stall, line 186) and fails the same way under the
same freeze (3 of 3), so it is in scope.

## Approach

Replace each thin wall-clock ceiling with an ordering fact that does not depend on host speed,
following the wall-clock-assert policy (`scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py`, ticket
`faintish-bumbling-tadpole`), which prefers a structural proxy over a timing budget:

1. `test_tool_timeout_cancels_an_async_tool`: keep the 5 s `asyncio.sleep` tool and the
   `cancelled` flag (set only in the tool's `CancelledError` handler, so it proves the sleep did
   not complete). Drop `elapsed < 4.5`. Add a proof that the cancellation came from the
   configured `tool_timeout`: pydantic-ai's `FunctionToolset.call_tool` wraps the call in
   `anyio.fail_after(timeout)` and turns the timeout into
   `ModelRetry(f'Timed out after {timeout} seconds.')`
   (`pydantic_ai/toolsets/function.py:653-656`, pydantic-ai 1.107.9), which reaches the model's
   second turn as a `RetryPromptPart` for tool `slow`. Assert that part exists and names
   `0.3`. Keep `"done" in result.output`.
2. `test_stalled_server_trips_read_timeout_under_run_sync`: make the stub server park on a
   `threading.Event` that the test sets only after `run_sync` returns (bounded wait of 30 s so
   the server thread always exits), instead of `time.sleep(5.0)`. The server then cannot answer
   or close before the client gives up, so `httpx.ReadTimeout` in the exception chain proves the
   client aborted the stalled read itself. Drop `elapsed < 4.5`.
3. Keep `test_slow_but_alive_server_completes_under_read_timeout`'s generous 20 s hang-guard
   unchanged; its ceiling is 100x the 0.15 s server delay.

Hangs stay bounded without the removed ceilings: if `tool_timeout` stopped working, the tool's
5 s sleep completes and `assert cancelled` fails; if the read timeout stopped working, the server
closes the connection at its 30 s bound and the chain holds no `ReadTimeout`; the pytest ini's
300 s per-test watchdog (`pyproject.toml:772-773`) backs both.

## Scope

- `tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py` — the two tests above. No `src/` change: the measured
  cancellation path is correct.

## Testing

- Before: with the scratch freeze plugin (4.5 s SIGSTOP 0.1 s into the call phase) on py3.11, both
  tests fail with `elapsed` asserts while `cancelled` / `ReadTimeout` hold (recorded above).
- After: the same freeze plugin, same interpreter, 3 runs: both tests pass.
- Mutation checks (scratch only, reverted): remove `tool_timeout=0.3` from the agent and the tool
  test fails on `assert cancelled`; raise the client `read` timeout above the server's park
  window (stub server releases at 1 s, `read=5`) and the read-timeout test fails because the
  chain holds no `ReadTimeout`.
- `pytest tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py` on py3.12 (`.venv`) and py3.11 with `-n 4`, then
  `make lint` (which runs the wall-clock-assert gate) and `make typecheck`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The cause of the >4 s elapsed time is identified with a reproduction: the freeze
      reproduction fails the unmodified test 3 of 3 runs with `assert cancelled` passing, and the
      in-suite samples show the cancel landing 0.300-0.303 s after tool start.
- [ ] The test no longer fails for that cause, without loosening its proof that the async tool
      is cancelled before its 5 s sleep completes: under the same 4.5 s freeze on py3.11 both
      tests pass 3 of 3 runs, and the tool test still asserts `cancelled` plus a
      `RetryPromptPart` for `slow` naming the 0.3 s timeout.
- [ ] `test_stalled_server_trips_read_timeout_under_run_sync` asserts the `ReadTimeout` against a
      server that cannot respond before the client aborts, with no wall-clock ceiling.
- [ ] Each mutation check in Testing turns its test red, and the restored test is green.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.

file_impact.reason: replace two thin wall-clock ceilings with ordering facts that do not depend on host speed
